type ModelEntry struct { ModelName string Model string APIKey string APIBase string RoutingStrategy string Fallbacks []string Weight int RPM int TPM int SimulateStatus int } type ChatResult struct { Content string ReasoningContent string Provider string Model string RequestID string CostMicros int64 RoutingMicros int64 CacheStatus string RouteReason string FallbackAttempted bool // Usage and Raw are omitted because their concrete types come from internal packages. } type ChatRequest struct { Model string Messages []Message Temperature *float64 TopP *float64 MaxTokens *int Stop []string Stream bool ReasoningEffort string User string } type Message struct { Role string Content string Name string ToolCallID string ToolCalls []ToolCall } type ToolCall struct { ID string Type string Function FunctionCall } type FunctionCall struct { Name string Arguments string } The ChatResult excerpt shows the stable top-level fields most applications need. It also has Usage and Raw fields whose concrete types come from internal packages; prefer top-level fields when you need to avoid depending on those implementation types. JSON tags are omitted here for readability; consult the source for serialization details.

func (c *Client) CreateVirtualKey(ctx context.Context, req VirtualKeyRequest) (*VirtualKeyInfo, error) func (c *Client) RevokeVirtualKey(ctx context.Context, keyID string) error func (c *Client) AddMCPServer(ctx context.Context, srv MCPServerConfig) (string, error) func (c *Client) SyncMCPTools(ctx context.Context, serverID string) (int, error) func (c *Client) ListMCPTools(ctx context.Context, route string) ([]map[string]any, error) func (c *Client) AddA2AAgent(ctx context.Context, agent A2AAgentConfig) (string, error) The corresponding public configuration types are VirtualKeyRequest, VirtualKeyInfo, MCPServerConfig, and A2AAgentConfig. Use the SDK feature guides for examples and required server permissions: Client configuration Virtual keys and FinOps MCP and A2A

The SDK includes public configuration types for registering MCP servers and A2A agents. The gateway exposes the protocol routes for tool calls, agent messages, and tasks. Administrative registration methods require a client authenticated with an admin key and the corresponding server permissions.

serverID, err := gw.AddMCPServer(ctx, gateway.MCPServerConfig{ Name: "Example tools", Slug: "example-tools", Transport: "streamable_http", URL: "https://tools.example.com/mcp", Enabled: true, }) if err != nil { return err } toolCount, err := gw.SyncMCPTools(ctx, serverID) if err != nil { return err } fmt.Printf("Synced %d tools\n", toolCount) The gateway applies outbound network policy to the MCP server URL. Confirm the transport and endpoint path expected by your MCP server before registering it.
documents.s: Register and sync an MCP server

documents.t: ListMCPTools accepts an empty route for the virtual hub, a server slug, or a toolsets/{slug} route: tools, err := gw.ListMCPTools(ctx, "example-tools") if err != nil { return err } for _, tool := range tools { fmt.Println(tool["name"], tool["description"]) } The gateway also provides a plain REST bridge for clients that do not use JSON-RPC. See the MCP overview, hub and REST bridge, and MCP API reference.

agentID, err := gw.AddA2AAgent(ctx, gateway.A2AAgentConfig{ Name: "Research agent", Slug: "research", Description: "Internal research agent", EndpointURL: "https://agent.example.com", }) if err != nil { return err } fmt.Println("Registered agent:", agentID) Use the A2A API reference for message and task request schemas. The SDK's SendA2AMessage method currently accepts a protobuf type from an internal package, so applications outside the gateway module should use the HTTP API or another supported public client for dispatch.

Use an admin client only for registration and management calls; use scoped virtual keys for application traffic. Allow only destinations that should receive gateway requests, and review the outbound SSRF/network policy. Disable Stdio MCP servers unless the gateway configuration and deployment are prepared to allow them.

Package: github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/pkg/gateway. The SDK provides a Go client for chat requests and common gateway operations. It can start a gateway instance in the current process or connect to an HTTP gateway service.

Mode Constructor What it does Embedded gateway.New(...) Loads gateway configuration, starts an in-process gateway server, and returns a client that talks to it over HTTP. Remote gateway.NewClient(url, key) or gateway.WithRemote(url, key) Sends requests to an already running gateway service. The embedded mode does not require a separately deployed gateway service. It still runs the gateway server and uses HTTP internally; it is not a direct function call into the inference handler.
The upstream module currently declares Go 1.26.0 in go.mod. Use a compatible Go toolchain: go get github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/pkg/gateway@v1.0.0

ctx := context.Background() gw, err := gateway.New( gateway.WithModelList(gateway.ModelEntry{ ModelName: "fast", Model: "gemini/gemini-2.5-flash", APIKey: "os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY", }), gateway.WithDemoMocksIfEnvMissing(), ) if err != nil { return err } defer gw.Close() result, err := gw.Chat(ctx, "fast", "Explain what an AI gateway does.") if err != nil { return err } fmt.Println(result.Content) This is a function-body example; it assumes context, fmt, and the gateway package are imported and is inside a function that can return an error. The mock option provides a local fallback when the referenced environment key is unset. To verify a real provider call, configure a valid key and omit the mock option.
Client configuration Chat and streaming Virtual keys and FinOps MCP and A2A Public SDK types and methods

The SDK provides methods for creating and revoking virtual keys and reading the spend summary. These are administrative operations: use a client configured with the gateway admin credential and protect it as a privileged object.

key, err := adminClient.CreateVirtualKey(ctx, gateway.VirtualKeyRequest{ Name: "payments-service", OrgID: "org_default", Role: "service_account", MaxBudgetMicros: 25_000_000, // 25 USD RPMLimit: 120, TPMLimit: 100_000, AllowedModels: []string{"fast"}, }) if err != nil { return err } // Store key.Key in an approved secret store; do not log or commit it. fmt.Println("Created key ID:", key.ID) MaxBudgetMicros uses micro-dollars (1 USD = 1,000,000 µ$). The returned key.Key contains the new secret and is only available in the creation response. Store it securely.

For server-controlled application code, create a request client using the virtual key: tenantClient := gateway.NewClient(gatewayURL, key.Key) result, err := tenantClient.Chat(ctx, "fast", "Summarize the supplied text.") WithKey can also copy a client with a different inference key. Keep any client carrying an admin credential inside trusted server code: the copy retains the original admin key for administrative methods.

if err := adminClient.RevokeVirtualKey(ctx, key.ID); err != nil { return err } The SDK calls the gateway's revoke endpoint. Subsequent authentication behavior depends on the gateway version and cache propagation; check the response and logs if a key still appears active.

summary, err := adminClient.SpendSummary(ctx) if err != nil { return err } fmt.Printf("Requests: %d; tokens: %d; cost: %d µ$\n", summary.TotalRequests, summary.TotalTokens, summary.TotalCostMicros) fmt.Println("Spend by provider:", summary.SpendByProvider) The summary type currently comes from an internal gateway package, although the SDK method exposes it. The stable JSON API is available at GET /admin/v1/spend/summary; see the cost accounting guide and API reference.
